summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — PTC +33%, ILMN +8%, CRL +7%, MRNA +7%, WDC +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CHRW -11%, LEN -7%, CMG -5%, BMY -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: PTC (+33.49%) — Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal at about $205/share (~$20B). The stock jumped on the reported takeover talks and closed at 192.26. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: PTC is a ~$21B large-cap industrial software name that no strategy's universe includes. It was also a gap-driven M&A pop, so a post-open signal would arrive late, and the stock sits just below the deal price.

top_movers.catalyst: Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal at about $205/share (~$20B). The stock jumped on the reported takeover talks and closed at 192.26.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: PTC is a ~$21B large-cap industrial software name that no strategy's universe includes. It was also a gap-driven M&A pop, so a post-open signal would arrive late, and the stock sits just below the deal price.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive M&A rule that admits any US name with a ≥+15% gap and a headline containing 'acquire' or 'takeover' to the universe, but only as a merger-arb hold capped below the offer price, with a small position size.

top_movers.catalyst: Analysts raised price targets on expected clinical-sales improvement and new catalysts. Gene sequencing is increasingly seen as AI infrastructure. The stock hit a new 52-week high near $294 after FY EPS guidance was raised.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ILMN is a mid/large-cap life-science tools name, and no strategy includes it. The move was a gradual analyst/narrative re-rating, not an earnings gap. The stock was already up about 119% YTD, so RSI-style filters would likely have excluded it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic momentum-universe rule that admits any US stock making a new 52-week high with ≥+5% on ≥1.5× 20-day average volume, even if it isn't in the static universe. Also consider adding healthcare/life-science tools names to the static list.

top_movers.catalyst: Investor Day: CRL set 2030 targets (low-double-digit adj. EPS growth, multi-year cost savings via automation) and guided 2026 EPS/revenue to the top of its ranges on biopharma demand recovery. Sources date the move Oct 5.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CRL is a mid-cap life-science CRO/tools name. It was also a scheduled-event gap-and-run, and the +7% move came mostly in the afternoon after the Investor Day, so pre-market and open signals gave no entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap healthcare tools/CRO names (CRL, MEDP, ICLR) to the news-reactive universe. Add an Investor Day/guidance-raise trigger that enters on an intraday gain of ≥+4% on ≥1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: Rally continued ahead of Moderna's Nasdaq-100 entry (replacing WBD, effective Oct 9) and its Oct 24 ESMO Phase 3 cancer-vaccine data with Merck; the stock is up ~500% YTD.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: a ~$75B large-cap biotech that rose ~500% YTD, so it was likely excluded by sector or universe rules. A parabolic run-up with extreme RSI would also fail mean-reversion and overbought filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'pending index inclusion / binary catalyst' watchlist (e.g. Nasdaq-100 adds within 5 days) to the momentum universe, with a capped position size and an RSI>85 override. Skip it if the sector is deliberately excluded.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Oct 6 catalyst. The +6.34% to $441.64 matches MarketBeat's 'jumps 6.3%' note dated Oct 5 (rebound after the Oct 2 selloff). Oct 6 coverage has WDC down ~6% on Toshiba/Seagate HDD news, so the date may be misaligned.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: WDC is a ~$150B+ mega-cap storage/AI-hardware name that no strategy lists. The move was a sector rebound after a sharp drop, with no gap-up or earnings signal for a momentum or news bot to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a high-beta AI-hardware group (WDC, STX, MU, SNDK) to the momentum universe, and check that the mover feed's close-to-close date matches the session; Oct 6 reports show WDC falling, not rising.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh news found for Oct 6. Search results point to a rebound after a 9-day losing streak, with AXON/e-commerce growth narrative and analyst support. Stock is still down ~58% YTD.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: APP is a large-cap, high-beta ad-tech name that no strategy includes. It was also in a months-long downtrend, so a momentum filter would have excluded it, and the +5% bounce looks like a dip-buy rather than a breakout.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta mega/large-cap tech like APP to the mean-reversion universe, with a trigger such as a ≥5% up day after ≥8 consecutive down days, and cap position size for its volatility.

top_movers.catalyst: Announced a $5.8B cash-and-stock acquisition of RXO (~43% stock, rest new debt). Investors worried about dilution, leverage and integration, and the stock fell ~11% to 140.61.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (no strategy includes it): a mid/large-cap NASDAQ logistics name. It was also an M&A-announcement gap-down, which a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot would skip or couldn't short. Sources date the drop to Oct 5, so the move was already priced in.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive watchlist rule that admits any S&P 400/500 name with an acquirer-side M&A headline and a gap ≤ -8% on ≥2× avg volume, for post-deal-drop mean-reversion longs only after a 2-day stabilization check.

top_movers.catalyst: Hunterbrook short report alleged Lennar hit quarterly targets by selling ~700 finished homes (~$200M) to its spinoff Millrose; the stock fell to a 52-week low on top of a weak housing backdrop.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid/large-cap homebuilder, not in any universe list). It was also a sudden short-report event, and a long-only momentum or mean-reversion bot has no way to profit from a gap down.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive 'short-report/governance' flag that blocks new longs and raises alerts on names gapping ≤-5% on a short-seller headline; no universe change is needed, since short-selling isn't supported.

top_movers.catalyst: No single hard catalyst found: renewed food-safety (produce-linked illness) headlines, beef/freight margin worries and caution before Q3 earnings on Oct 28 drove a ~4.7% drop.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CMG is a mid-priced (~$31) large-cap restaurant name that no strategy includes. The drop was a gradual headline-driven slide with no earnings gap or volume spike for a momentum or news filter to catch.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change: this was a sentiment-driven drop in a name outside the universe, and expressing it needs short capability the bot lacks. If wanted, add consumer-discretionary large caps to the mean-reversion universe, but with an earnings-proximity block (skip within ~14 days of results).

top_movers.catalyst: Leerink Partners downgraded BMY from Outperform to Market Perform and cut its price target to $59 from $73, citing pipeline doubts (milvexian, admilparant) ahead of upcoming clinical readouts. Some sources date the drop to Oct 5.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BMY is a large-cap pharma name that no strategy includes. The drop was a single-analyst downgrade with a modest -3.8% move on a low-beta defensive stock, so it likely wouldn't clear gap or volume-spike filters anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap healthcare names such as BMY to the news-reactive universe, and treat analyst downgrades with a price-target cut of 15% or more as an entry trigger or a no-buy veto for the following session.
